# FaceAuth — Rust-based Facial Recognition System

*⚠️ **AI-Generated Code Notice**: This project documentation and code have been generated by AI. Review thoroughly before production use, as AI-generated code may contain errors, security vulnerabilities, or incomplete implementations. Test extensively and consider security audits.*

FaceAuth is a Linux facial authentication system written in Rust, inspired by [Howdy](https://github.com/boltgolt/howdy). It unlocks `sudo`, polkit prompts, screen lockers or logins through PAM with a webcam or a Windows Hello-style IR camera. Face authentication is always an **additional** path: when it fails or is skipped, PAM falls through to your password.

## Features

- **Face detection** with SCRFD-2.5GF (5 landmarks, preferred), then YuNet, Ultra-Light or a Haar cascade as fallbacks. SCRFD letterboxes the frame into a square canvas, so 16:9 IR frames are not stretched; YuNet runs at each frame's own size.
- **Alignment** via a 5-point least-squares affine transform to the InsightFace canonical pose.
- **Embeddings** from EdgeFace-S (512-dim) via OpenVINO (NPU / GPU / CPU) or tract-onnx on CPU; MobileFaceNet is still supported through `[recognition]`.
- **Fail-closed matching**: no substitute embeddings when the model is missing or inference fails; the recognizer fingerprint is stored with enrolled samples and checked on every attempt.
- **Robust decisions**: `required_matches` consecutive matching frames, score = mean of the `top_k` nearest samples, optional IR liveness gate against screens.
- **Quality-checked enrollment**: blur and pose filters, near-duplicate rejection, and guidance to cover left / frontal / right head poses.
- **Root-only model store** (`/var/lib/faceauth/models`), atomic writes, symlink and permission checks.
- **Skips remote sessions** (SSH, `PAM_RHOST`) and a closed lid.
- **Tools**: `faceauth doctor` (camera, IR emitter, models, NPU, storage, PAM), `faceauth calibrate` (threshold tuning), `faceauth-ui` (Russian / English GUI with live guidance, live test and model management).

## Security model

- `faceauth-auth` runs as root from `pam_exec`. It only trusts model files that are **owned by root, mode 0600, not symlinks**, in a root-owned `0700` directory. Earlier versions kept models in `~/.local/share/faceauth`, where anyone with access to your unlocked session could replace your face with theirs and then pass `sudo`.
- Writing or reading models requires root: `sudo faceauth …` from the CLI; `faceauth-ui` goes through `pkexec` (polkit `auth_self_keep`, i.e. your password), and under `pkexec` faceauth only touches the caller's own model.
- Remote sessions are skipped (`[auth] skip_remote`), so a `sudo` typed over SSH cannot be approved by whoever sits in front of the laptop.
- The IR liveness check (`[liveness]`) rejects faces that look like a screen in IR. It does **not** stop a printed photo. Treat face auth as a convenience factor, not a replacement for your password.
- Run `faceauth` as root only with the system config: as root, `./faceauth.toml` in the working directory is ignored (use `--config` explicitly).

## Installation (Arch Linux)

### Dependencies

- **opencv** 4.11+ or 5.x (Arch currently ships 5.0; `build.rs` detects the version), **v4l-utils**, **pam**
- **rust**, **cargo**, **clang**, **llvm** to build
- optional: **openvino** (AUR) for NPU/GPU, **intel-npu-driver** (≥ 1.30 on Lunar Lake), **linux-enable-ir-emitter**, **polkit** for the GUI

### PKGBUILD

```bash
makepkg -si
```

Installs:
- `/usr/bin/faceauth`, `/usr/bin/faceauth-auth`, `/usr/bin/faceauth-ui`
- `/usr/share/faceauth/models/*.onnx`
- `/etc/faceauth/config.toml` (commented copy in `/usr/share/doc/faceauth/config.toml`)
- `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/faceauth.conf` (creates `/var/lib/faceauth` and `/var/cache/faceauth`)
- `/usr/share/polkit-1/actions/org.faceauth.policy`
- `/usr/share/doc/faceauth/pam-example`

### From source

```bash
cargo build --release
sudo install -Dm755 target/release/faceauth target/release/faceauth-auth target/release/faceauth-ui -t /usr/bin/
sudo install -Dm644 models/*.onnx -t /usr/share/faceauth/models/
sudo install -Dm644 packaging/config.toml /etc/faceauth/config.toml
sudo install -Dm644 packaging/faceauth.tmpfiles /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/faceauth.conf && sudo systemd-tmpfiles --create faceauth.conf
sudo install -Dm644 packaging/org.faceauth.policy -t /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/
```

Build without OpenVINO: `cargo build --release --no-default-features`.

## Quick start

```bash
sudo faceauth doctor                 # camera, IR emitter, models, NPU, storage, PAM
sudo faceauth add -u "$USER"         # enroll 9 samples with pose guidance
sudo faceauth test -u "$USER"        # run the real authentication loop
sudo faceauth calibrate -u "$USER"   # measure your scores, suggest distance_threshold
```

Then add PAM (below). Or do everything from `faceauth-ui` → **Setup**.

## PAM configuration

Put this line **first** in the `auth` section of `/etc/pam.d/sudo` (or `polkit-1`, your screen locker, `system-auth`):

```
auth  sufficient  pam_exec.so quiet /usr/bin/faceauth-auth
```

`sufficient`: a recognized face finishes authentication, anything else continues to your password line. The user comes from `PAM_USER`; do **not** write `-u $USER` (PAM does not expand shell variables). See [pam/faceauth](pam/faceauth).

### `faceauth-auth` exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Face matched |
| 10 | Skipped: disabled (`faceauth disable`), remote session, lid closed, or no model enrolled |
| 11 | No match before `[video] timeout` |
| 12 | Setup error: config, camera, models, or an untrusted model file |
| 13 | Every frame was too dark (IR emitter off?) |

## Commands

All commands that read or change models need root.

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `faceauth add -u USER [-s 9] [--append] [--variant NAME] [-d DEVICE] [--ir]` | Enroll. `-d` defaults to `video.device_path`, the camera `faceauth-auth` uses |
| `faceauth list [USER] [--json]` | Show models (samples, variants, recognizer fingerprint) |
| `faceauth remove -u USER [--variant NAME]` | Remove a variant, or the whole model |
| `faceauth rename-variant -u USER OLD NEW` | Rename a variant |
| `faceauth clear -u USER` | Delete all face data of the user |
| `faceauth disable` / `enable` | Globally skip / re-enable face auth (`/etc/faceauth/disabled`) |
| `faceauth test -u USER [--timeout S] [--ir]` | Run the authentication loop and print a report |
| `faceauth calibrate -u USER [--frames 40]` | Score your own face, suggest a threshold, show IR face brightness |
| `faceauth migrate -u USER [--force]` | Move a ≤ 0.2 model from `~/.local/share/faceauth` into the root store |
| `faceauth doctor [-u USER] [--json]` | Diagnostics with hints |
| `faceauth test-camera [-d DEVICE]` | Print frame darkness |
| `faceauth config -o FILE` | Write a default config |
| `faceauth import` / `verify -u USER` | Used by `faceauth-ui` through `pkexec` (JSON on stdin) |

`--config FILE` works with every command (not via pkexec).

### Appearance variants

A model has a **primary** sample set and named **variants** (e.g. `glasses`); authentication uses the best-matching set.

| Action | Example |
|--------|---------|
| Replace the whole model (drops variants) | `sudo faceauth add -u USER` |
| Append to the primary set | `sudo faceauth add -u USER --append` |
| Replace / create a variant | `sudo faceauth add -u USER --variant glasses` |
| Append to a variant | `sudo faceauth add -u USER --variant glasses --append` |

## IR cameras and login in the dark

1. Find the IR node: `v4l2-ctl --list-devices` (or `faceauth doctor`, which marks monochrome cameras).
2. In `/etc/faceauth/config.toml`:
   ```toml
   [video]
   device_path = "/dev/video2"
   ir_mode = true
   ```
3. Enroll and authenticate on the same IR device: `sudo faceauth add -u "$USER"`.

If frames are black, the IR emitter is probably off: try [linux-enable-ir-emitter](https://github.com/EmixamPP/linux-enable-ir-emitter). `ir_mode` disables the darkness filter and relaxes Haar. With `[liveness] ir_check`, faces that are too dark or flat in IR (screens) are rejected; `faceauth calibrate` prints your face brightness so you can tune `min_face_brightness` / `min_face_stddev`.

EdgeFace was trained mostly on RGB, so IR scores are usually different — calibrate instead of guessing a threshold.

## OpenVINO / Intel NPU

With the `openvino` feature (default) and `use_openvino = true`, models run through OpenVINO:

```toml
[openvino]
device = "AUTO"                          # AUTO, NPU, GPU or CPU
cache_dir = "/var/cache/faceauth/openvino"
```

- `AUTO` uses NPU/GPU when present and starts on CPU while the accelerator compiles the model, which matters because `faceauth-auth` starts fresh on every `sudo`. Without accelerators it uses plain CPU.
- Compiled models are cached in `cache_dir` (falls back to `~/.cache/faceauth/openvino` when not writable), so later attempts skip compilation.
- `faceauth doctor` shows the device actually used and load / first-inference times, also on CPU for comparison. Small models like EdgeFace are fast on CPU too; the NPU pays off once the cache is warm.
- Models exported with a dynamic input shape (EdgeFace's `batch_size`, SCRFD's `H`/`W`) are reshaped to a static `[1, 3, H, W]` before compiling — the NPU compiler crashes on partially dynamic graphs otherwise.
- Install the runtime from the AUR (`openvino` or `openvino-bin`); the crate links it at runtime.

Enrollment and authentication may use different devices (same model file), but scores can differ slightly.

## Graphical interface (`faceauth-ui`)

- Russian or English depending on `LANG` (override with `FACEAUTH_LANG=ru|en`).
- Camera picker (IR cameras marked), live preview with a target oval and hints (move closer, hold still, turn left/right…).
- **Enroll**: new model or add to the existing one, into the main set or a variant.
- **Test**: live score against your threshold and the consecutive-match streak.
- **Models**: samples per set, rename / delete variants, delete the model.
- **Setup**: runs `faceauth doctor` and shows the PAM line to copy.

The window captures as your user; saving and checking go through `pkexec faceauth …` (one password prompt, then cached by polkit).

## Configuration

See the commented [packaging/config.toml](packaging/config.toml). Every key is optional. The CLI and GUI look for `./faceauth.toml` → `~/.config/faceauth/config.toml` → `/etc/faceauth/config.toml`; as root only `/etc/faceauth/config.toml` is used. Relative model paths resolve against the config file's directory; missing ones fall back to `/usr/share/faceauth/models`.

Detection order is SCRFD → YuNet → Ultra-Light → Haar: `create_detector` takes the first model that loads, so a missing `scrfd_path` simply falls back to the old stack.

- `scrfd_2.5g_kps.onnx` (SCRFD-2.5GF with landmarks) is shipped for detection; `scrfd_input_size` (default 640, rounded up to a multiple of 32) sets its input.
- `edgeface_s_gamma_05.onnx` (EdgeFace-S, 512-dim) is the default recognizer. `[recognition] normalization` must match the model: `"unit"` for EdgeFace, `"insightface"` for MobileFaceNet/ArcFace; an unknown value fails closed instead of silently mis-normalizing.
- YuNet: `face_detection_yunet_2023mar.onnx` is shipped and works on OpenCV 4.x and 5.0 (checked on Arch's OpenCV 5.0 with per-frame input sizes). A `2026may` export (dynamic input shape) can be configured instead; if it fails to load, the `2023mar` file next to it is used.

`dark_threshold` is `100 − mean brightness` in percent: the default 85 only skips RGB frames with a mean brightness below ~38/255.

## Upgrading from 0.3 (new models)

- 0.4 switches to SCRFD detection + EdgeFace recognition. Embeddings from a different recognizer are **not** comparable, so re-enroll every user: `sudo faceauth add -u "$USER"`, then `sudo faceauth calibrate -u "$USER"`.
- Old configs keep working without edits: they keep YuNet/MobileFaceNet (the new keys default to the old behaviour); add the new keys from [packaging/config.toml](packaging/config.toml) to switch.

## Upgrading from 0.2

- Models moved from `~/.local/share/faceauth/models` to `/var/lib/faceauth/models` and are no longer read from home. Run `sudo faceauth migrate -u "$USER"` (or re-enroll), then delete the old file.
- Migrated models have no recognizer fingerprint; re-enrolling adds it.
- Default model paths moved to `/usr/share/faceauth/models`; old `/etc/faceauth/models` paths keep working through the fallback.
- New config sections (`[liveness]`, `[openvino]`, `[auth]`, `[enroll]`) have defaults; removed keys (`certainty`, `embedding_size`, `save_failed`, `save_successful`) are ignored.

## Development

```
src/
├── authenticate.rs      # authentication loop (PAM helper + `faceauth test`)
├── camera.rs            # V4L2 capture, rotation, scaling, ROI statistics
├── config.rs            # TOML config, discovery, defaults
├── database.rs          # models, merge logic, root-only storage, GUI payloads
├── detection.rs         # SCRFD / YuNet / Ultra-Light / Haar, NMS, clipping, pose estimates
├── devices.rs           # /dev/video* discovery
├── diagnostics.rs       # `doctor` result types
├── doctor.rs            # `faceauth doctor`
├── enroll.rs            # step-wise enrollment session
├── i18n.rs              # ru/en messages
├── matching.rs          # distances, top-k, streak tracker, pose collector, fingerprints
├── openvino_backend.rs  # OpenVINO session (AUTO, cache, latency hint)
├── pipeline.rs          # capture → detect → analyze → embed
├── privilege.rs         # root / pkexec checks, passwd lookup
├── recognition.rs       # alignment + embeddings (OpenVINO / tract)
├── session.rs           # remote-session and lid checks
├── verdict.rs           # per-frame verdicts
├── main.rs              # CLI
└── bin/
    ├── auth.rs          # PAM helper
    └── ui/              # GUI (main.rs) + camera worker (worker.rs)
```

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test
cargo test --no-default-features
```

CI runs the same on Arch Linux (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `build.rs` sets `cfg(opencv5)` when `pkg-config` finds `opencv5` (override with `FACEAUTH_OPENCV_MAJOR=4|5`) to follow API moves: `CascadeClassifier` lives in `xobjdetect` and `warpAffine` takes an `AlgorithmHint` on OpenCV 5.
